title: Establish LTS compatibility charter and automated upgrade matrix across runtime, API, SDKs, and Console
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Define a practical LTS compatibility charter and generate an automated, machine-readable upgrade matrix that maps compatible combinations of: serving runtime builds, public REST API minor/patch releases, official SDK major/minor versions, and Console releases. This ticket covers charter definition, verification checks, deprecation policy, and the first-pass automation that emits a compatibility artifact consumed by the release pipeline. Scope includes hosted API, Dedicated runtime images, official SDKs (Python/Node/Go), and Redwood Console only. Out of scope: partner integrations and third-party community SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented LTS charter describing support windows, deprecation policy, and versioning rules for runtime, API, SDKs, and Console. 2) A generator job that produces a JSON compatibility matrix for each candidate release and uploads to internal artifact storage. 3) CI gate that fails canary promotion when compatibility tests (runtime smoke + SDK integration tests against API contract) fail. 4) Migration notes template produced for each breaking change. 5) Security review flagged and scheduled before first LTS branch cut.
deliverables: CI gating config and canary promotion policy
rollout_gates: Gates: 1) Pre-cut: automated compatibility generator runs against candidate builds and verifies no API contract regressions. 2) Canary: deploy to 1% of traffic with SDK integration tests and monitoring for error/latency regressions for 48h. 3) Gradual rollout stages (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with automated rollback on predefined SLO breaches. 4) Manual approval required for any gate with customer-impacting deprecations.
test_plan: - Unit tests for generator and matrix schema. - Integration tests: run each official SDK against staging runtime + API surface. - Regression harness: replay 50 representative prompts from eval suite to detect semantic regressions. - Performance smoke: 95th percentile latency baseline check. - Backwards-compatibility harness: exercise deprecated endpoints and feature flags to confirm deprecation signage and migration guidance are surfaced.
migration_guidance: Define migration paths per change type. For non-backwards-compatible API changes: provide conversion snippets in each official SDK, recommended runtime pinning strategies, and automated changelog generation. For runtime-only changes (kernel/quantization), provide SDK compatibility guarantees and opt-in flags to exercise new behavior behind feature gates.
monitoring_and_alerting: Matrix artifact must include telemetry keys to enable targeted dashboards. Key alerts: API contract errors, SDK integration failures, canary latency/throughput regressions, increased 5xx rates on rollback threshold. Instrumentation: add trace tags for 'compat-matrix-version' and expose per-route canary percentages in Console.
